title: Tarte Tropezienne
subtitle: The Provencal brioche filled with orange blossom creme diplomate
excerpt: La Tarte Tropezienne is a thick disc of sugar-topped brioche sliced open and filled with creme diplomate scented with orange blossom water. It is the signature pastry of Saint-Tropez. The brioche must be very soft and pillowy; the cream must be cold and light. The combination of warm-temperature bread and cold cream is the point.
sourceNotes: Tarte Tropezienne was created in 1955 by Alexandre Micka, a Polish pastry chef who opened a shop in Saint-Tropez. The recipe was made famous when Brigitte Bardot tasted it during the filming of And God Created Woman. The original recipe is kept secret, but the form (soft brioche + orange blossom cream) is standard in published French pastry references.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bake the brioche the day before. Fill with cream on the day of serving; the cream softens the brioche too quickly if left overnight.

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: Conventional oven, 190 degrees Celsius. Fan oven: 175 degrees Celsius. Middle shelf. The brioche is quite thick and needs 22 to 25 minutes.

glossaryTerms.definition: Creme patissiere folded with whipped cream. Lighter than creme patissiere alone, it holds its shape when piped but has a delicate, mousse-like texture. Orange blossom water or vanilla is folded in with the cream. It must be cold when assembled and cannot be left at room temperature for long.

content.text: must be made ahead and chilled before filling. The brioche must be warm or at room temperature. Keep the two separate until the moment of assembly; the contrast between the yielding, slightly warm bread and the cold cream is what defines the texture.

items.prepNote: for scattering on top before baking

content.text: Combine flour, yeast, sugar, and salt. Add the warm milk and eggs and bring together into a rough dough. Knead for 5 minutes. Add the softened butter in three stages, kneading each addition in fully. Knead for a further 8 minutes until very smooth and elastic.

Cover and leave at room temperature for 1 hour until doubled. Press into a greased 23 cm round tin to a depth of about 3 cm. Proof for a further 1 hour until very puffy. Scatter pearl sugar across the surface. Bake at 190 degrees Celsius for 22 to 25 minutes until deep golden. Cool completely before filling.

Make creme patissiere from the milk, yolks, sugar, and cornflour. Stir in the orange blossom water. Press cling film onto the surface and refrigerate until cold. When ready to assemble, beat the cold creme patissiere until smooth, then fold in the whipped cream in two additions.

Slice the cooled brioche in half horizontally. Spoon or pipe the creme diplomate generously onto the bottom half; it should be a thick, domed layer, not a thin spread. Set the top half on the cream and press gently. Dust with icing sugar and serve the same day.
